cells.tense: You are steady now with what changed, and you are the one keeping it steady.
cells.ask: Pass one piece of it to someone this week as an exchange, not a gift, and let what they hand back count for something.
cells.core:
You're living in what the change left. Something ended, something got made in the clearing, and you're holding it steady — not clutching, not rushing it out the door. That holding is the work right now, and it's going well. The thing stays available to you instead of sealed off.

The part that's next: let some of it leave your hands. Not because it's finished, because holding something well eventually means putting it where it can move. Fair exchange between people is a plain skill you're already near. When you pass part of this along, do it as an exchange and not a gift, and leave room for the other side to bring something back to you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what the change made. Time to let some of it move.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this that hasn't arrived, guarding a shape nobody is threatening yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're protecting and leave it alone for three days — let it shift or don't, and watch what happens without you holding it.
cells.core:
You're guarding what the change produced, and the guard duty has gone past the thing. Talks about it turn into checks on whether it's still intact. You're defending against a threat that's mostly out in front of you — someone's going to take it, misuse it, get it wrong — and you're spending the whole present getting ready for that.

Care is what's underneath the grip, and the care is sound. On a good day here, the thing can sit in a room without you and still be yours when you come back. Preservation isn't the same as holding on. What you made wants to keep moving through what it is. The grip is the problem, not the care.

cells.tense: You were standing at the threshold when the change finished, and some part of you is still there.
cells.ask: Write one sentence about what actually changed, read it to someone who was around for the ending, and hear your own voice say it.
cells.core:
The change happened and you stepped back from it. You saw what got made in the clearing, and you've been keeping it off to the side like it might not be real, or not yours, or not ready for the light. What's underneath isn't doubt about the thing. It's the standing-still itself.

There's a way of living here that doesn't need certainty about what you are — you just keep taking your own shape around people, and the shape holds. The ground hasn't moved out from under you. Your direction is still there, and it doesn't want proof, it wants your weight on it. There's a sentence about what changed that you haven't let yourself finish. Finish it out loud, and hear what your voice does.

cells.tense: You are already holding steady what changed, and you have never said that's what you're doing.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, about one thing you've made steady, 'I'm the one holding this.' Just that, no explanation.
cells.core:
Look at what's around you — the structure, the routine, the way people know what to expect. You built the container the change needed to land in, and you built it without announcing it. You call it just keeping things running. Keeping shape is real work and it has your hand all over it.

The done-well version looks like this: things make sense around you, and that stops surprising you. What's absent isn't the grip — it's the credit. Keeping this steady has your name on it and you've been filing it under circumstances. Say it in your own voice, once, without softening it down, and let that be the whole statement.
